thread:
jess-cs: FYI MeridianBio onboarding tomorrow 08:00 UTC. Procurement asked for a one-page SLO + credit process they can add to their vendor packet.

nina-pm: Do we have the exact SLO phrasing they signed? I think it's 99.8 monthly avail + p95 gen <= 400ms, but want to be exact.

jess-cs: Contract says 99.8% availability monthly and p95 latency <= 400ms for /v1/generate. Also they want the pro-rata credit rule for mid-month starts.

li-sales: Procurement flagged two things: 1) they need an easy example calculation, 2) they want confirmation we won't share payload data during evidence collection.

tom-sre: I'll draft a short ops playbook and a sanitized CSV schema for evidence. Our current test p95 for their baseline load ~ 360ms, availability last 14d 99.92.

jess-cs: Important: they want any credit applied within the next invoice cycle, and a documented timeline for requests (we should include 30-day claims window).

tom-sre: Draft playbook snippet:```SLO + CREDITS SUMMARY
- Availability: >= 99.8% per calendar month
- Latency: p95 <= 400ms per calendar month (generation routes)

EVIDENCE FOR CLAIMS
- Metrics export (CSV/JSON) showing uptime windows and per-request latency
- Error-rate graphs and request_ids for affected intervals
- Incident timeline and remediation notes from SRE

CREDIT TIERS (plain english)
- If monthly availability is between 99.0% and 99.8% => 15% credit of that month
- If monthly availability is below 99.0% => 40% credit of that month
- Latency breaches: credit applies only when p95 > 400ms for > 6 consecutive hours and error rate increased > 1%

CLAIM PROCESS
- File claim within 30 days with evidence bundle
- We review within 10 business days and apply credit on next invoice cycle
```

li-sales: Can you include a short example with numbers for their $12k monthly bill? Procurement loves those.

tom-sre: Example: $12,000 monthly -> 15% credit = $1,800; 40% credit = $4,800. I'll put that in plain text.

jess-cs: Add a partial-month pro-rata example: if they start mid-month we prorate by days active in month (e.g., start on 16th of 30-day month -> billed for 15/30 days). Credits are likewise prorated to that billed amount.

nina-pm: Also include a short privacy sentence: we only share request IDs and aggregate metrics unless customer explicitly approves payload-level logs via DPA amendment. Keep it non-legal.

tom-sre: Adding a sample CSV header for their engineers to validate ingestion:```CSV_HEADERS
timestamp,route,model,request_id,status_code,latency_ms,region,customer_tag
2026-03-20T07:59:01Z,/v1/generate,redwood-g,req-abc123,200,378,us-east-1,meridianbio
```

incidents-bot: incidents-bot: alert-config updated for meridianbio (p95 alert -> 380ms)

li-sales: Procurement also asked for a short SLA exceptions paragraph (maintenance, force majeure, DDoS etc.). Keep concise.

jess-cs: Draft exception: scheduled maintenance with >=48h notice excluded; emergency mitigations notified within 1h may have a short mitigation window (up to 30 minutes) excluded from creditable downtime; force majeure and customer-side misconfigurations are excluded.

tom-sre: Note: for model cold-start or node replacement events we document start/end and exclude a 15-minute automatic mitigation window if we acted immediately and communicated on the incident channel.

nina-pm: Great. Next steps: tom finalizes playbook + CSV sample (EOD), jess drafts the one-page SLO doc and procurement-friendly paragraph (tomorrow morning), li confirms recorded enablement slot with customer.

li-sales: MeridianBio wants a recorded 45-min walkthrough Tues 10:00 PDT. I'm setting a calendar invite and will ask for recording consent.

jess-cs: Thanks everyone. Once docs are ready I'll send to procurement and post the PDF here. If renewal risk shows up after go-live we escalate to head of CS. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: note: dashboard share link prepared (redwood/grafana/meridianbio)
